features.name: Synchronised division volley fire
features.summary: When a musket division is set to volley mode, every soldier in it raises and holds his musket until the whole division is aimed, then all fire together on the next frame; soldiers without a musket in hand are made to draw one.
features.mechanics: mst:sp_campaign_*/t5 (every frame) calls volley_fire. For each team (0/1) and each of 9 divisions it checks the storage troop trp_custom_battle_dummy (455) slot 60+div (team 0) / 70+div (team 1) == 2 (volley mode, written by give_mm_order from the F6 'firing' sub-menu). Phase slot 80+div / 90+div: phase 0 = 'make ready' -> agent_set_attack_action(agent,0,1) (ready and hold) for every human of that team+division whose agent slot 23 == 0 (not routed) and who is not >1 m from his scripted destination (i.e. still marching); any agent wielding a non-musket (item slot 1 != 12) is switched to a musket from inventory. If every agent reached the aimed-hold attack state (attack_action 5) the phase flips to 1 = 'fire' -> agent_set_attack_action(agent,0,0) releases everybody at once, then the phase flips back to 0.
evidence: explain nw volley_fire: 5 direct callers, all mst:sp_campaign_*/t5 [every 0s], bare-int call_script
dis nw volley_fire: slot 60/70 eq 2 test, phase slot 80/90, agent_set_attack_action 0,1 then 0,0
writer of slot 60+div: give_mm_order (l0==2 branch troop_set_slot 455 :l5 :l1)

features.name: Musket-line formations via invisible locator props (line/column/square/skirmish, wheel)
features.summary: Each division gets an invisible anchor prop. Orders move or rotate the anchor and every soldier is given an exact scripted spot around it: a line 2-4 ranks deep, a marching column, a hollow-ish square (side = sqrt(n)) or an open skirmish line, and the block can wheel 45 degrees left/right or turn to face the enemy.
features.mechanics: mst:sp_campaign_*/t2 (once) spawns 20 copies of spr_formation_locator (prop 1560, one per team x division, invisible) and moves them to entry points; scene-independent because it uses spawn_scene_prop at runtime. On spawn/death correct_num_troops_in_formation keeps a live head-count per division in trp_custom_battle_dummy slots 20-38. give_mm_order (from the F4/F5 order presentation) writes the movement order (slot 100+div/110+div: 0 hold-here, 1 follow, 2 charge, 3 advance, 5 fall back) and the formation shape (slot 40+div/50+div: 0 line, 1 column, 2 square, 3 skirmish) and $g_wheel (1 left, 2 right, 3 face enemy). deploy_division_via_teleport (238 stmts; called from per-mission one-shot/state triggers t15/t19/t33) moves the locator (to the player for 'follow', +/-1.8 m for advance/fall back, rotated for wheel), then computes rank width from head-count (>59 -> n/4 per rank, >29 -> n/3, >5 -> n/2), spacing 100 (200 for skirmish, with staggered second rank) and gives each agent agent_set_scripted_destination (or _no_attack when the division is in hold-fire mode).

features.name: F-key order tree with 'hold where I look' arrow
features.summary: Pressing F4 opens a small order overlay: F4 again = movement (hold at the spot you are looking at, shown by a ground arrow while the key is held; follow; charge; advance; halt; fall back; retreat; slow/quick march), F5 = formation (line, column, square, skirmish, wheel left/right, face enemy), F6 = firing (fire at will / volley / hold).

Its ti_on_presentation_run (t1) reads F4-F12 and calls give_mm_order(menu, order, team). Orders are applied only to divisions selected in the Native order UI (class_is_listening_order) and echoed as '<division>, form square!' etc.

features.name: Player-crewed artillery (12pdr, howitzer, mortar, fort, naval, carronade, swivel, rocket)
features.summary: Cannons are multi-part scene props the player walks up to and works step by step with use-buttons (sponge/load cartridge, load round/shell/canister/bomb, ram, aim, fire, limber to a horse); once 'controlling' a gun the player aims with the camera and fires with a key, and the ball flies, bounces, damages people and destructible props.
features.mechanics: Cannon kinds are scene props 1482-1489 (spr_mm_cannon_12pdr_wood ... spr_mm_cannon_rocket_wood) with child props (wheels, barrel, limber, buttons). Button props (spr_mm_aim_button, spr_mm_load_cartridge_button, spr_mm_round_button, spr_mm_limber_button, ...) call use_item on ti_on_scene_prop_use; use_item is gated (this_or_next|multiplayer_is_server)(neg|game_in_multiplayer_mode) so it also runs in single player. A mission trigger (mst:tutorial/t9) reads game keys 6/7 while $g_currently_controlling_object==1 and, when not in multiplayer, calls handle_agent_control_command directly (SP branch) which sets agent slot 6 (5 = fire). mst:tutorial/t1 (every 0.5 s, same SP-inclusive guard) aims the barrel from agent_get_look_position and, on command 5, calls fire_cannon; recoil_cannon animates the recoil. mst:tutorial/t2 (every 0.125 s) moves balls: cannon_ball_hit_ground (bounce), cannon_explosion_on_position / explosion_at_position, deliver_damage_to_prop. State lives in ~60 scene-prop slots (6-50+) and agent slots 6/7.

features.name: Grenades, explosive shot and destructible props
features.summary: Thrown grenades and explosive bullets blow up on impact, hurting nearby people and chipping damage off destructible scenery (doors, walls, gabions, crates), which steps through damage stages until it collapses; explosive supply crates chain-explode.

features.name: Central muzzle flash, smoke and report on every gunshot (engine hook)
features.summary: Every time any firearm is discharged the game plays the right report sound and puffs muzzle smoke and flash at the barrel, scaled per weapon class (pistol, musket, rifle, blunderbuss), with lighter smoke for the player's own shot so his view is not blinded; bullet impacts throw dust/spark particles.
features.mechanics: game_missile_launch is an engine callback (params: shooter agent, weapon item, missile item) - NW defines it so the engine calls it on every missile launch. It picks sound 164/165/166 and smoke offsets by weapon id band, scales the burst to 65% when the shooter is the local player (client_get_my_agent), and fires particle_system_burst_no_sync 65-68. Impacts: item triggers on itm_bullets, itm_pistol_ammo, itm_canister_ammo, itm_shell_fragment call mm_on_bullet_hit (psys 90/91 at pos63).
evidence: dis nw game_missile_launch (62 stmts) - sound + 4 particle bursts

features.name: Division-level line-battle AI (advance to range, halt and fire, charge when close)
features.summary: In NW's custom battles the AI handles each of its nine divisions separately: a division that can see an enemy division within about 200 m halts and fires at will, one that gets within 20 m (or is cavalry) charges, divisions out of contact hold with fire-on-command, and if nobody is engaged the army eventually switches to a general advance.
features.mechanics: mst:quick_battle_battle/t17 (once) -> select_battle_tactic -> select_battle_tactic_aux (306 stmts: tallies infantry/cavalry/skirmish/artillery head-counts per side from trp_custom_battle_dummy_2 (456) slots 0-17/72-89 written by the custom-battle designer) and battle_tactic_init -> battle_tactic_init_aux. mst:quick_battle_battle/t20 (every 5 s) -> battle_tactic_apply -> battle_tactic_apply_aux (304): for each own division, find nearest enemy division (division_get_average_position) and line of sight (position_has_line_of_sight_to_position at +2 m); in LOS and <200 m or enemy within 25 m (get_closest3_distance_of_enemies_at_pos1) -> if cavalry or <20 m team_give_order charge (2) else hold at current spot + fire at will (13); otherwise hold + fire on command (17). With no division engaged a random roll against mission time switches tactic to 4 (advance) and stamps $g_last_tactic_change_at. mst:quick_battle_battle/t21 (every 1 s) re-issues charge/hold per division from slot 90+div/99+div.

features.name: Courage, rout and rally per soldier (with retreat order and difficulty scale)
features.summary: Each soldier starts with a courage score (scaled by a campaign difficulty modifier for the player's side); deaths nearby lower it, enemy deaths raise it, a soldier whose courage falls below a threshold that rises as he loses health runs away, and he can rally if courage recovers. Ordering a division to 'retreat' makes it rout on purpose.
features.mechanics: ti_on_agent_spawn (mst:sp_campaign_*/t1) sets agent slot 24 = 3000-4000 (x $g_global_morale_modifier/10 for team 0) and slot 23 = 0. ti_on_agent_killed_or_wounded (t3) -> apply_death_effect_on_courage_scores: counts same-team agents within 13 m of the casualty, then for every agent within 100 m adds a distance-weighted delta (+10 for enemies; -15+nearby_count capped at -5 for friends, divided by 3 if the casualty was already routing) to slot 24. Every 3 s after 25 s (t9) -> decide_run_away_or_not: if the division's movement order is retreat (mordr 14) or courage < 3500 - 40*hp -> agent_start_running_away + slot 23 = 1; if routed and courage >= 3700 - 40*hp and no retreat order -> agent_stop_running_away (rally).
evidence: dis nw decide_run_away_or_not (36 stmts) - retreat order 14 and rally branch
dis nw mst:sp_campaign_vienna/t1:conseq stmts 5-14

features.name: Shouted voice commands and order call-outs
features.summary: The player (and officers) can shout a voice command with a key; NPC soldiers and officers audibly call out orders when the player issues them, with nationality- and gender-appropriate voice sets and a cooldown that is shorter for officers.
features.mechanics: mst:quick_battle_battle/t0 (every frame, key 43 = voice-command key) -> if not multiplayer calls multiplayer_server_agent_play_voicecommand(agent, cmd) directly (SP branch); t1 (ti_on_order_issued) makes agents of the ordered divisions shout. The script (178 stmts, guard this_or_next|multiplayer_is_server / neg|game_in_multiplayer_mode) checks agent slot 1 (last shout time) against $g_time_between_voice_commands(_officer) by troop rank slot 12 (3-5 = officers), picks a voice set from troop faction/troop range and player gender, and plays the sound at the agent. Musicians and pianists are excluded.

features.name: Post-battle results screen with kill-based pay and casualty tally
features.summary: After each scripted battle a results screen lists enemies killed, the player's personal kills, allies and companions lost, and the money earned: +20 per personal kill, +10 per enemy killed by the army, -5 per soldier lost, -10 per companion lost; the player can accept or retry.

features.summary: NW's single-player mode is a fixed chain of battles (Vienna bridge, Austerlitz, Dresden x2): a campaign map, a briefing, a walk-around camp with merchants and companions, a companion and companion-equipment picker, scripted fly-over camera intros with letterbox bars and timed objectives, and a memoir screen.

features.summary: Each NW map rolls weather and time: time of day, rain/snow strength, cloud cover and fog distance/colour, so the same field can be fought at dawn in fog or at noon in rain.
